name: Regional Cancer Centre (RCC), Thiruvananthapuram
tagline: Kerala’s principal public oncology centre with comprehensive cancer care
summary: State-run comprehensive cancer institute on the Medical College campus, offering diagnosis, radiotherapy, medical and surgical oncology, research and training.
description: Regional Cancer Centre (RCC), Thiruvananthapuram is Kerala’s principal public oncology institute. It provides comprehensive cancer diagnosis, medical and surgical oncology, radiotherapy, nuclear medicine and allied supportive services.

RCC combines clinical services with research, training and community oncology. It is an autonomous state‑and‑central government sponsored centre that handles large outpatient and inpatient volumes and runs postgraduate and diploma training programmes in oncology disciplines.

In 2026 the centre expanded into a new multi‑storey block to centralise advanced services (radiotherapy, nuclear medicine, bone marrow transplant, operating theatres and ICUs) and reduce waiting times for patients. RCC continues to operate from its Medical College Campus location with outreach into district services and palliative care networks.
highlights: Comprehensive services: radiation oncology, medical oncology, surgical oncology, pediatric oncology
New multi‑storey block with radiotherapy, nuclear medicine and bone marrow transplant facilities (operational 2026)
Teaching and training: diploma and postgraduate oncology programmes
Strong community oncology & palliative care outreach across Kerala
Research programmes and clinical trials in cancer epidemiology and treatment

sections.heading: Background
body: RCC is an autonomous state/central sponsored cancer institute located on the Medical College Campus (Ulloor) in Thiruvananthapuram. The centre developed as Kerala’s main public referral centre for cancer care, combining clinical services with research, training and community oncology.

Over decades RCC has built divisions in radiation, medical and surgical oncology supported by pathology, radiology, nuclear medicine, microbiology, transfusion medicine, palliative care and cancer epidemiology. It also hosts training courses such as oncology nursing and DNB programmes.

sections.heading: Clinical services and capabilities
body: RCC provides diagnostics (pathology, imaging, nuclear medicine), systemic therapy (medical oncology/chemotherapy), surgical oncology (including advanced and minimally invasive procedures) and radiotherapy. The centre supports allied services such as blood bank, microbiology, pain and palliative care, stoma and rehabilitation clinics.

The new multi‑storey building that became operational in 2026 adds centralised radiotherapy facilities, nuclear medicine wards, a bone marrow transplant unit, multiple operation theatres, ICUs and additional inpatient beds to reduce waiting times and expand capacity.

sections.heading: Research, training and outreach
body: RCC runs cancer research and epidemiology programmes, participates in clinical trials, and provides postgraduate and diploma training in oncology disciplines and oncology nursing. The centre also leads community oncology initiatives and collaborates with district hospitals to expand screening, early detection and palliative services across Kerala.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: RCC is on the Government Medical College campus (Medical College PO, Ulloor, Thiruvananthapuram, PIN 695011). For appointments and outpatient clinic timings confirm with the centre before travel; busy caseloads mean scheduled appointments are strongly recommended.

Reach the campus by taxi or local bus from Thiruvananthapuram city. For major procedures or admissions follow the referral and admission instructions provided by RCC; patients often need referral documents, prior imaging and blood reports for faster processing.

latest.text: Kerala government reports the RCC’s new multi‑storey building (₹242 crore) has become operational, adding radiotherapy, nuclear medicine, bone marrow transplant unit, OTs, ICUs and 200 new beds to the centre.

News coverage ahead of the official inauguration noted the new multi‑storey building and listed planned services including linear accelerators, nuclear medicine wards, bone marrow transplant and operation theatres.

Kerala’s Annual Plan 2025–26 sets out the new RCC block (14 storeys / 2.75 lakh sq ft) and details equipment and units planned: 2 linear accelerators, CT/MR simulators, 10‑bed BMT unit, 6 modular OTs, nuclear medicine ward and a robotic surgery unit.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Year‑round; clinical services are continuous — confirm outpatient/clinic timings before you travel.
visitorInfo.howToReach: On the Medical College Campus (Ulloor), Thiruvananthapuram (PIN 695011). Reach by taxi or local bus from the city; the campus is a short (around 5–10 km) drive from the central railway station and the international airport — confirm local travel times.
etiquette: Book appointments in advance and carry prior imaging and referral documents to speed triage.
Expect high patient volumes—arrive early for outpatient clinics and reconfirm timings.
Ask about financial support schemes or concessions if cost is a concern; the centre runs public-sector rates and support services.
Follow hospital instructions on visiting hours and infection control; bring a family member to help with navigation and paperwork.
